web_evidence.note: A Cardiff University doctoral thesis reproduces sustained first-person prose from the novel and identifies Huw Morgan as the retrospective narrator who recalls his boyhood and traces the valley's transformation.

search_log: Searched: "How Green Was My Valley" Richard Llewellyn first person narrator Huw Morgan point of view; opened explicit point-of-view analyses from BookRags and SuperSummary.

Searched title and author with excerpt, first chapter, and full-text terms; found a library record at Open Library and a limited Google Books preview, but neither exposed a sustained searchable chapter in the opened page.
Searched publisher sources at Penguin and Penguin Random House; Penguin's description confirms Huw's retrospective memories but does not explicitly name grammatical person.

Searched scholarly and university-hosted material for narrator and narrative technique; opened a Cardiff University thesis containing first-person novel prose and an explicit structural identification of Huw as the retrospective narrator.
Targeted searches for epistolary, frame, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view produced no credible evidence of sustained narration in another person.
person_note: The base narration is Huw Morgan's retrospective first-person account of his own childhood and community. Multiple event quotes independently expose his participation through 'I,' 'me,' and 'my,' while scholarly and explicit whole-book web descriptions identify Huw as narrator and protagonist. Apparent second person in the quotations is direct address to deceased relatives or generic gnomic 'you,' not a second-person protagonist. Third-person descriptions of family members remain compatible with Huw observing them and do not form an autonomous third-person strand. No credible evidence indicates alternating narration; the main residual limitation is that the accessible library and publisher previews did not provide a continuous full chapter.
